title: Paul at the Areopagus / Mars Hill: the unknown-god speech + the Aratus quote

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — earliest substantial manuscript witnesses (Codex Vaticanus B/03 + Codex Sinaiticus א/01, 4th c. CE); SBLGNT base text; cross-collated against P45 (Chester Beatty I, ~250 CE) and the Western text of Codex Bezae (D/05, 5th c.) for Acts-specific variants. Acts 17:28 preserves a verbatim citation of Aratus *Phaenomena* line 5 (3rd c. BCE).

paragraphs.text: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, ὅπου ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
paragraphs.translit: Diodeusantes de tēn Amphipolin kai tēn Apollōnian ēlthon eis Thessalonikēn, hopou ēn synagōgē tōn Ioudaiōn.

i18n.en: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.

paragraphs.text: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτούς, καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν,
paragraphs.translit: kata de to eiōthos tō Paulō eisēlthen pros autous, kai epi sabbata tria dielexato autois apo tōn graphōn,

i18n.en: And according to Paul's custom, he went in to them, and on three Sabbaths reasoned with them from the scriptures,

paragraphs.text: διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός, ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: dianoigōn kai paratithemenos hoti ton christon edei pathein kai anastēnai ek nekrōn, kai hoti houtos estin ho christos, ho Iēsous hon egō katangellō hymin.

i18n.en: opening and setting forth that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and "this Jesus whom I proclaim to you is the Christ."

paragraphs.text: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων πλῆθος πολὺ γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai tines ex autōn epeisthēsan kai proseklērōthēsan tō Paulō kai tō Sila, tōn te sebomenōn Hellēnōn plēthos poly gynaikōn te tōn prōtōn ouk oligai.

i18n.en: And some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a great multitude of the devout Greeks and not a few of the leading women.

paragraphs.text: Ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι τῶν ἀγοραίων ἄνδρας τινὰς πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἐπιστάντες τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον·
paragraphs.translit: Zēlōsantes de hoi Ioudaioi kai proslabomenoi tōn agoraiōn andras tinas ponērous kai ochlopoiēsantes ethorouboun tēn polin, kai epistantes tē oikia Iasonos ezētoun autous proagagein eis ton dēmon·

i18n.en: But the Jews, becoming jealous, took along some wicked men of the marketplace, and gathering a crowd, set the city in an uproar; and assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.

paragraphs.text: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας, βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν,
paragraphs.translit: mē heurontes de autous esyron Iasona kai tinas adelphous epi tous politarchas, boōntes hoti Hoi tēn oikoumenēn anastatōsantes houtoi kai enthade pareisin,

i18n.en: But when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some of the brothers before the city authorities, shouting: "These men who have turned the world upside down have come here also,

notes.official: Thessalonica (vv.1-9): *politarchas* 'city-rulers' (v.6) is a Macedonian-specific civic-official-term confirmed by inscriptional evidence from Thessalonica (the title is attested in 1st-c. Macedonian inscriptions). The Lukan-Acts narrative's use of the specific term is one of the philological-historical-precision features that Witherington 1998 + Keener 2014 cite as evidence for the Lukan-Acts historiographical-reliability.

paragraphs.text: οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων· καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσι, βασιλέα ἕτερον λέγοντες εἶναι Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: hous hypodedektai Iasōn· kai houtoi pantes apenanti tōn dogmatōn Kaisaros prassousi, basilea heteron legontes einai Iēsoun.

i18n.en: and Jason has received them; and they all act against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."

paragraphs.text: ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα,
paragraphs.translit: etaraxan de ton ochlon kai tous politarchas akouontas tauta,

i18n.en: And they disturbed the crowd and the city authorities when they heard these things.

paragraphs.text: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai labontes to hikanon para tou Iasonos kai tōn loipōn apelysan autous.

i18n.en: And taking security from Jason and the rest, they released them.

paragraphs.text: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν, οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi de adelphoi eutheōs dia nyktos exepempsan ton te Paulon kai ton Silan eis Beroian, hoitines paragenomenoi eis tēn synagōgēn tōn Ioudaiōn apēesan.

i18n.en: And the brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, who, upon arriving, went into the synagogue of the Jews.

paragraphs.text: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ, οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας, καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως.
paragraphs.translit: houtoi de ēsan eugenesteroi tōn en Thessalonikē, hoitines edexanto ton logon meta pasēs prothymias, kath’ hēmeran anakrinontes tas graphas ei echoi tauta houtōs.

i18n.en: Now these were more noble-minded than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all eagerness, examining the scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

notes.official: The Berean engagement (vv.10-15): the 'noble Bereans' (*eugenesteroi* v.11) examining the scriptures daily 'whether these things were so'. The narrative establishes a positive-Lukan-Acts model of receptive-but-critical engagement with the apostolic-message.

paragraphs.text: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι.
paragraphs.translit: polloi men oun ex autōn episteusan, kai tōn Hellēnidōn gynaikōn tōn euschēmonōn kai andrōn ouk oligoi.

i18n.en: Therefore many of them believed, along with not a few prominent Greek women and men.

paragraphs.text: Ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ, ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες καὶ ταράσσοντες τοὺς ὄχλους.
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de egnōsan hoi apo tēs Thessalonikēs Ioudaioi hoti kai en tē Beroia katēngelē hypo tou Paulou ho logos tou theou, ēlthon kakei saleuontes kai tarassontes tous ochlous.

i18n.en: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul in Berea also, they came there too, stirring up and disturbing the crowds.

paragraphs.text: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν· ὑπέμεινάν τε ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: eutheōs de tote ton Paulon exapesteilan hoi adelphoi poreuesthai heōs epi tēn thalassan· hypemeinan te ho te Silas kai ho Timotheos ekei.

i18n.en: And then the brothers immediately sent Paul off to go as far as the sea, but Silas and Timothy remained there.

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν, καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de kathistanontes ton Paulon ēgagon heōs Athēnōn, kai labontes entolēn pros ton Silan kai ton Timotheon hina hōs tachista elthōsin pros auton exēesan.

i18n.en: Those who conducted Paul brought him as far as Athens, and after receiving a command for Silas and Timothy to come to him as quickly as possible, they departed.

paragraphs.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου, παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν.
paragraphs.translit: En de tais Athēnais ekdechomenou autous tou Paulou, parōxyneto to pneuma autou en autō theōrountos kateidōlon ousan tēn polin.

i18n.en: Now while Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he observed that the city was full of idols.

paragraphs.text: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας.
paragraphs.translit: dielegeto men oun en tē synagōgē tois Ioudaiois kai tois sebomenois kai en tē agora kata pasan hēmeran pros tous paratynchanontas.

i18n.en: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.

paragraphs.text: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρείων καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ, καί τινες ἔλεγον· Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν; οἱ δέ· Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι· ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο.
paragraphs.translit: tines de kai tōn Epikoureiōn kai Stoikōn philosophōn syneballon autō, kai tines elegon· Ti an theloi ho spermologos houtos legein? hoi de· Xenōn daimoniōn dokei katangeleus einai· hoti ton Iēsoun kai tēn anastasin euēngelizeto.

i18n.en: And some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also conversed with him. And some said: "What does this babbler want to say?" But others: "He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign divinities" — because he was preaching Jesus and the resurrection.

paragraphs.text: ἐπιλαβόμενοί τε αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον Πάγον ἤγαγον λέγοντες· Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή;
paragraphs.translit: epilabomenoi te autou epi ton Areion Pagon ēgagon legontes· Dynametha gnōnai tis hē kainē hautē hē hypo sou laloumenē didachē?

i18n.en: And taking hold of him, they brought him to the Areopagus, saying: "May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?

paragraphs.text: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν· βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι τίνα θέλει ταῦτα εἶναι.
paragraphs.translit: xenizonta gar tina eispherein eis tas akoas hēmōn· boulometha oun gnōnai tina thelei tauta einai.

i18n.en: For you bring some strange things to our ears; we wish therefore to know what these things mean."

paragraphs.text: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ἢ ἀκούειν τι καινότερον.
paragraphs.translit: Athēnaioi de pantes kai hoi epidēmountes xenoi eis ouden heteron ēukairoun ē legein ti ē akouein ti kainoteron.

i18n.en: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners visiting there used to spend their time in nothing other than telling or hearing something new.

paragraphs.text: Σταθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη· Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ·
paragraphs.translit: Statheis de Paulos en mesō tou Areiou Pagou ephē· Andres Athēnaioi, kata panta hōs deisidaimonesterous hymas theōrō·

i18n.en: So Paul, standing in the midst of the Areopagus, said: "Men of Athens, I observe that in every way you are very religious.

notes.official: **MAJOR AREOPAGUS SPEECH — vv.22-31.** Paul's natural-theology framework speech to the Athenian Areopagus court. The longest extended NT speech to a non-Jewish-non-Christian audience and the most-systematic Pauline engagement with Greek philosophical / poetic-tradition. Cross-corpus to Aratus *Phaenomena* line 5 (verbatim citation at v.28b) + Epimenides *Cretica* (citation at v.28a) + Stoic-Cleanthean *Hymn to Zeus*. Documented at central-glossary entry `areopagus-speech-acts-17-22-31-natural-theology-aratus-epimenides-cross-corpus`. The Raëlian-canon engagement is acknowledged-without-endorsement per the established framework.

paragraphs.text: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο· Ἀγνώστῳ θεῷ. ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε, τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: dierchomenos gar kai anatheōrōn ta sebasmata hymōn heuron kai bōmon en hō epegegrapto· Agnōstō theō. ho oun agnoountes eusebeite, touto egō katangellō hymin.

i18n.en: For as I was passing through and observing your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: 'To an unknown god.' What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.

notes.official: *agnōstō theō* 'to an unknown god'. Pausanias *Description of Greece* 1.1.4 reports altars to 'unknown gods' (theois agnōstois) on the road from Phaleron to Athens; Philostratus *Vit. Apoll.* 6.3.5 similarly attests Athenian altars 'even to unknown gods' (kai agnōstōn daimonōn). The plural altars are well-attested; the Lukan-Acts singular ('to AN unknown god') may be Lukan-redactional or may reflect a specific altar Paul encountered. Diogenes Laertius Lives 1.110 reports that Epimenides advised the Athenians to sacrifice 'to the appropriate god' without specifying which god, to avert a plague — the historical-religious-context for the unknown-god altar tradition.

paragraphs.text: ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ
paragraphs.translit: ho theos ho poiēsas ton kosmon kai panta ta en autō, houtos ouranou kai gēs hyparchōn kyrios ouk en cheiropoiētois naois katoikei

i18n.en: The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands,

notes.official: The natural-theology framework (vv.24-29): God-as-creator (v.24) + God-not-served-by-human-hands (v.25 anti-anthropomorphism) + all-peoples-from-one (v.26 acts-of-God-in-history) + universal-seeking-of-God (v.27 *kataskēptōsin* 'might grope for' anthropology) + the Epimenidean and Aratean citations (v.28) supporting the in-him-we-live framework.

paragraphs.text: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·
paragraphs.translit: oude hypo cheirōn anthrōpinōn therapeuetai prosdeomenos tinos, autos didous pasi zōēn kai pnoēn kai ta panta·

i18n.en: nor is he served by human hands as though he needed anything, since he himself gives to all life and breath and everything.

paragraphs.text: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: epoiēsen te ex henos pan ethnos anthrōpōn katoikein epi pantos prosōpou tēs gēs, horisas prostetagmenous kairous kai tas horothesias tēs katoikias autōn,

i18n.en: And he made from one every nation of humanity to dwell on the whole face of the earth, having determined appointed times and the boundaries of their habitation,

paragraphs.text: ζητεῖν τὸν θεὸν εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν, καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα.
paragraphs.translit: zētein ton theon ei ara ge psēlaphēseian auton kai heuroien, kai ge ou makran apo henos hekastou hēmōn hyparchonta.

i18n.en: that they should seek God, if perhaps they might grope for him and find him — though indeed he is not far from each one of us.

paragraphs.text: Ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν, ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθ’ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν· Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν.
paragraphs.translit: En autō gar zōmen kai kinoumetha kai esmen, hōs kai tines tōn kath’ hymas poiētōn eirēkasin· Tou gar kai genos esmen.

i18n.en: For in him we live and move and have our being; as also some of your own poets have said: 'For we are also his offspring.'

notes.official: **MAJOR PHILOSOPHICAL-LITERARY CITATION SITE.** Two verbatim Greek-tradition citations in one verse: (i) *en autō gar zōmen kai kinoumetha kai esmen* 'for in him we live and move and have our being' (v.28a) — widely attributed to a *Cretica* of Epimenides (6th-c. BCE Cretan philosopher-prophet), preserved in Syriac quotation in Isho'dad of Merv c. 850 CE; same source cited at Titus 1:12 (the Cretans-are-always-liars verse); (ii) *tou gar kai genos esmen* 'for we are also his offspring' (v.28b) — verbatim from Aratus *Phaenomena* line 5 (3rd-c. BCE Stoic-astronomical-poem opening hymn to Zeus). Aratus was Cilician (from Soli, near Tarsus) — a compatriot of Paul. The Stoic Cleanthes *Hymn to Zeus* offers a parallel Stoic-framing. Documented at central-glossary entry `areopagus-speech-acts-17-22-31-natural-theology-aratus-epimenides-cross-corpus` and overlay-glossary entry `acts-17-28-aratus-quote-attribution-convention`.

paragraphs.text: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ, χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου, τὸ θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον.
paragraphs.translit: genos oun hyparchontes tou theou ouk opheilomen nomizein chrysō ē argyrō ē lithō, charagmati technēs kai enthymēseōs anthrōpou, to theion einai homoion.

i18n.en: Being therefore the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the divine is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by the art and imagination of man.

paragraphs.text: τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ θεὸς τὰ νῦν παραγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: tous men oun chronous tēs agnoias hyperidōn ho theos ta nyn parangellei tois anthrōpois pantas pantachou metanoein,

i18n.en: The times of ignorance, then, God overlooked, but now he commands all people everywhere to repent,

notes.official: The Christian-kerygmatic closing (vv.30-31): the call to universal repentance + the future-resurrection-judgment proclamation. The closing transitions from natural-theology to Christian-kerygma. The closing is rejected by part of the Areopagus audience (v.32 the resurrection mention provokes mockery) but accepted by some — including Dionysius the Areopagite and Damaris (v.34).

paragraphs.text: καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν, πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kathoti estēsen hēmeran en hē mellei krinein tēn oikoumenēn en dikaiosynē en andri hō hōrisen, pistin paraschōn pasin anastēsas auton ek nekrōn.

i18n.en: because he has fixed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed; and of this he has given assurance to all by raising him from the dead."

paragraphs.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἀκουσόμεθά σου περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν.
paragraphs.translit: akousantes de anastasin nekrōn hoi men echleuazon hoi de eipan· Akousometha sou peri toutou kai palin.

i18n.en: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked, but others said: "We will hear you again about this."

paragraphs.text: οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs ho Paulos exēlthen ek mesou autōn.

i18n.en: So Paul went out from their midst.

paragraphs.text: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν, ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: tines de andres kollēthentes autō episteusan, en hois kai Dionysios ho Areopagitēs kai gynē onomati Damaris kai heteroi syn autois.

i18n.en: But some men joined him and believed, among whom were Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

notes.official: Athenian converts (v.34): Dionysius the Areopagite — a member of the Areopagus court — is the most-prominent named convert. Later Christian tradition (the corpus pseudo-Dionysiacum, c. 500 CE) attributed a major mystical-theological corpus to this Dionysius, though the corpus is now widely-recognized as a 5th-6th-c. composition by an unknown author writing under the Dionysian pseudonym.
